items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: So this Manuel Marlowe, one of the leaders of my band, I had a couple of bands, of course, the leaders in all these bands.

ctx.x: Let them have their fun. Listen, how... There's a magazine section there when he was a couple of years old, I don't know how much, a couple of weeks ago. He states then that he had to hide a cornet that he had in the well in his home. Yes. How could he do such a thing? When the first... He didn't even know how to hold a cornet in his mouth when he played with... He used to sit in the Elmire Pleasure Ground... Well, he did. ...in the park. And Manuel Marlowe is the man that showed him how to blow the cornet.

He used to, you know, play, but not anywhere as good, you understand? So this Manuel Marlowe, one of the leaders of my band, I had a couple of bands, of course, the leaders in all these bands. I don't get it.
How they can tell such a thing?

items.title: Manuel Mello Interview, 1959-08-03
items.q: And Lance played trombone, I played cornet. Jack Lane played trap drums.

ctx.x: I haven't heard anything from him in a long time.

Boy, he got the swell head. Did he get a swell head? I had Martin Abraham to chink with me when he had one, two pair shoes. He had a pair of white shoes and a pair of black shoes and a pair of white pants and a pair of black pants. And that was all. That was all. He had a wife with about 40 kids. He used to live up in the jungles on Royal Strait. But I had Martin with me a good long time. Martin was a pretty good bass player. But the fellow that learned Martin how to play bass, and he had a good guitar player.…
